title: Smooth Diffeomorphisms and Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers
summary: A classical theorem of Maillet asserts that every nonconstant rational function over $\mathbb{Q}$ maps Liouville numbers to Liouville numbers. In 1984, Mahler asked whether a transcendental entire function can have the same property. We prove a strong smooth counterpart: writing $\mathscr{L}$ for the set of Liouville numbers, there exist orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, arbitrarily close to the identity and transcendental over $\mathbb{R}(x)$, such that for every real number field $K\subset\mathbb{R}$, every $n\geq 1$, and every $m\geq 0$, \[…
